h: Romans, lighthouses and a ferry ride
p: An hour or two is about right for the museum, which leaves you loads of time to explore the rest of South Shields. And there's a lot more history here than most people expect.

First up, head to Arbeia Roman Fort, a short walk away in the Lawe Top area. It was a supply base near the eastern end of Hadrian's Wall, and the reconstructed gateway, barrack block and commanding officer's house give you a real feel for frontier life. Pair it with the museum and you've got a cracking history day that won't break the bank.

Then make for the coast. Ocean Road links the town centre with the seafront and it's famous locally for its string of curry houses, so you won't be stuck for tea. Sandhaven Beach and Littlehaven give you big stretches of sand, and Ocean Beach Pleasure Park adds a bit of seaside fun for the kids. Walk out along the South Pier when the weather's kind and watch the ships coming in and out of the Tyne.

South of town, the coast road leads to Marsden Bay, with its towering limestone cliffs, seabirds and the famous Marsden Rock just offshore. Further along, the red and white Souter Lighthouse is a National Trust attraction in its own right.

Fancy something different? The Shields Ferry crosses the river to North Shields in a few minutes, which is a fun little trip for the kids and leads you to the Fish Quay. Coming by Metro is easy too, with South Shields at the end of the line.
